title: Compliance crosscheck pilot notes
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for a small pilot to exercise a subset of SOC2 controls, validate evidence collection ergonomics, and identify friction points before we scale to full sprint.

Context notes (to self):
- scope: hosted API + Dedicated control plane + Private (minimal) — pick 1 customer flow per deployment type. For pilot, focus on hosted + dedicated.
- goal: turn 5 high-value controls into repeatable playbooks (evidence path + ownership) in 2 weeks.
- non-goal: finished mapping for all systems — this is a fast feedback loop.

Controls shortlist (first-pass):
1) Logical access management (account provisioning + SSO) — C-AC-01
   - test idea: sample of 10 user accounts created in last 90 days; verify joiner/leaver tickets; confirm 2FA enforced; snapshot of IdP group membership.
   - quick evidence items: idp-audit-2026-02-01.csv, joiner-ticket-IDs.txt, sso-2fa-policy.png
   - owner candidate: Leo (eng-identity)

2) Change control for infra (code review + approved PRs) — C-CH-02
   - test idea: pick 3 infra changes touching serving-runtime in prod in last 6 months; confirm PRs have approvals + release notes + rollout policy recorded.
   - evidence: pr-543, pr-612, pr-678 (links), release-notes-2025-11.md, rollout-audit.log
   - friction risk: infra/ops sometimes use emergency bypass — need a log of bypass rationale.

3) Data encryption at rest (KMS integration) — C-CR-03
   - test idea: fetch KMS key policy, list of resources bound to key; demo decrypt flow (logs showing KMS ops).
   - evidence: kms-policy-2026-01.pdf, kms-access-audit-2026-02.csv
   - notes: private deployments may use HSM; need alternate evidence path.

4) Monitoring & alerting (SLO->oncall) — C-OP-04
   - test idea: pick 2 incidents in last year, verify pager duty runbook exec + postmortem + alert thresholds documented.
   - evidence: incident-2025-10-12.md, pd-runbook-serving-latency.pdf, alerts-def.json

5) Backup & restore cadence (storage resilience) — C-DR-05
   - test idea: sample backup job logs; confirm small restore test completed for dataset X (date, operator).
   - evidence: backup-jobs-logs-2026-01.tar, restore-test-notes-2026-02-20.txt

Quick mapping notes:
- Many docs currently live in engineering shared drive (shared_drives/engineering/*) — but auditors want single evidence bundles. Need a lightweight script to zip pointers + snapshots.
- Proposed evidence pack naming convention: redwood-evidence-<control>-<YYYYMMDD>-<owner>.zip

Practical friction items to capture during pilot (observations I want to validate):
- who actually owns the artifacts? (team-level vs person-level)
- are logs retained for the required window? (slo on retention?)
- how easy is it to extract a tamper-evident artifact (hash + metadata)?
- access gating: can we share evidence with an external auditor without exposing prod secrets? need temp credentials/obfuscation flow.

Mini runbook (pilot steps):
1) Kickoff sync (30m) — confirm control subset, owners, success criteria. -> target 2026-02-17
2) Evidence harvest (3 days) — owners collect artifacts, put into evidence-staging/ with README.
3) Reviewer pass (2 days) — trust-ops reviews completeness, flags gaps.
4) Tabletop demo (1 day) — run through an audit ask with an external friendly reviewer.
5) Retro & next actions (1 day) — produce pilot retro doc and automated tasks.

To-dos (me / Lyra):
- [ ] Draft email to owners with timeline and sample artifact checklist (send by 2026-02-16)
- [ ] Create evidence packaging script (zip + checksum + simple manifest) -> MVP 2026-02-20 (script name: bundle-evidence.sh)
- [ ] Book tabletop with Julian (external reviewer) for 2026-02-25
- [ ] Confirm data obfuscation checklist with security (Ivy)

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we require HSM/KMS audit logs for every private deployment sample or accept an attestation from infra? (trade-off: time vs confidence)
- How to treat ephemeral infra (ephemeral clusters for CI) — do we need to capture CI artifacts or only prod?
- Is there appetite for a lightweight attestation form for teams to sign off (one-pager + checkbox) vs full evidence?

Notes to self (rambling):
- 2x people have mentioned that the current service account naming is inconsistent; if owners can't find keys, evidence harvest will stall. Maybe add a quick inventory step.
- If we can get one clean bundle for change control + incident, that will prove the pattern for other controls. Prioritize those.
- Keep everything in users/ for the scratch, but final artifacts should be in shared_drives/ for traceability.

Example artifact checklist (copy in email):
- human-readable README (who, what, when, how to verify)
- raw logs (with redaction notes if needed)
- screenshots/snapshots of UI where applicable (IdP console, PD incident timeline)
- links to PRs + short context note
- manifest.json (list of files + SHA256 hashes)

Lightning notes on evidence automation:
- bundle-evidence.sh pseudocode: gather files -> compute shasum -> create manifest -> tar.gz -> compute final checksum -> upload to evidence-bucket (s3) with restricted ACLs -> record pointer in confluence page
- maybe use GitHub Actions for reproducible packaging triggered by a label (e.g., tag: evidence-ready).

Final quick plan for next 48h:
- send owner email, spin up evidence-staging folder, create initial README template, start bundle script skeleton.

End of scratchpad (will refine after kickoff).
